title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.

Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

"""Dataset loading + train/test splitting for the TokenCore reproduction.

Loads the released annotation files from ``repo/data/<name>.npy`` (dict with
keys ``sentences``, ``tokens``, ``labels``) exactly as the authors' notebooks do,
and implements the two candidate train/test protocols:

* ``split_authors``  - replica of ``split_anomaly_data`` from the authors'
  ``eval.py`` (recovered from git history, commit f26d62d): ``int(len(X)*0.5)``
  documents are drawn from the *normal* documents with
  ``np.random.seed(random_state); np.random.choice(...)``; everything else
  (remaining normal + all anomalous) is the test set.
* ``split_literal``  - literal reading of the paper's Section 6.1 ("50% normal
  documents as training data"): half of the *normal* documents are used for
  training.
"""

import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "repo"
DATA = REPO / "data"


def load_dataset(name):
    """Return (docs, doc_labels) where docs[i] = {'tokens': [...], 'labels': [...]}.

    Document label = 1 iff at least one token label is 1 (Definition 2, R11).
    """
    path = DATA / f"{name}.npy"
    data = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens = data["tokens"]
    labels = data["labels"]
    docs = []
    doc_labels = []
    for toks, labs in zip(tokens, labels):
        toks = [str(t) for t in toks]
        labs = [int(x) for x in labs]
        assert len(toks) == len(labs), "token/label length mismatch"
        docs.append({"tokens": toks, "labels": labs})
        doc_labels.append(1 if any(labs) else 0)
    return docs, np.array(doc_labels, dtype=int)


def split_authors(doc_labels, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42):
    """Verbatim replica of the authors' ``eval.split_anomaly_data`` index logic."""
    y = np.array(doc_labels)
    n_train = int(len(y) * train_ratio)
    normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
    np.random.seed(random_state)
    train_indices = np.random.choice(normal_indices, size=n_train, replace=False)
    test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(y)), train_indices)
    return np.asarray(train_indices), np.asarray(test_indices)


def split_literal(doc_labels, seed=0, normal_ratio=0.5):
    """Half of the *normal* documents are used for training (paper Section 6.1)."""
    y = np.array(doc_labels)
    normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    perm = rng.permutation(normal_indices)
    n_train = int(len(normal_indices) * normal_ratio)
    train_indices = np.sort(perm[:n_train])
    test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(y)), train_indices)
    return np.asarray(train_indices), np.asarray(test_indices)


def dataset_stats(docs, doc_labels):
    n_tokens = sum(len(d["tokens"]) for d in docs)
    n_pos = sum(sum(d["labels"]) for d in docs)
    return {
        "n_docs": len(docs),
        "n_anomalous_docs": int(doc_labels.sum()),
        "anomaly_doc_rate": float(doc_labels.mean()),
        "n_tokens": n_tokens,
        "n_positive_tokens": n_pos,
        "positive_token_rate": n_pos / max(n_tokens, 1),
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for name in ["grammar", "restaurant_review", "sms_spam"]:
        docs, dl = load_dataset(name)
        st = dataset_stats(docs, dl)
        print(name, st)
        for fn in ("split_authors", "split_literal"):
            tr, te = split_authors(dl) if fn == "split_authors" else split_literal(dl)
            n_tr_tok = sum(len(docs[i]["tokens"]) for i in tr)
            n_te_tok = sum(len(docs[i]["tokens"]) for i in te)
            n_te_pos = sum(sum(docs[i]["labels"]) for i in te)
            print(f"  {fn}: train_docs={len(tr)} test_docs={len(te)} "
                  f"train_tokens={n_tr_tok} test_tokens={n_te_tok} "
                  f"test_pos_tokens={n_te_pos} train_anom_docs={int(dl[tr].sum())}")

"""BERT-base word-level embedding extraction with max pooling over subwords.

Reimplements (and vectorises) the authors' ``align.extract_word_embeddings``
(repo/align.py, byte-wise identical logic to ``align2.py`` recovered from git
history): take the last hidden state, drop special tokens, group WordPiece
subwords by ``word_ids()`` and take the element-wise maximum over the subwords
of each word (paper Eq. 1, R2/R9).  Each produced word unit keeps the gold token
string and label of the word it was built from, so the alignment is 1:1 with the
token annotation.
"""

import numpy as np
import torch


def build_model_and_tokenizer(model_name, device="cpu"):
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return tokenizer, model


def extract_docs(docs, model_name="bert-base-cased", device="cpu", batch_size=32,
                 max_length=512, verbose=False):
    """Extract word-level embeddings for a list of documents.

    Returns a list (one entry per document) of dicts::

        {"tokens": [...], "labels": [...], "embeddings": np.ndarray (n_words, 768)}

    The i-th embedding corresponds to ``tokens[i]`` / ``labels[i]``.
    """
    tokenizer, model = build_model_and_tokenizer(model_name, device=device)
    out = []
    n_batches = (len(docs) + batch_size - 1) // batch_size
    for b in range(n_batches):
        batch = docs[b * batch_size:(b + 1) * batch_size]
        texts = [d["tokens"] for d in batch]
        enc = tokenizer(texts, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                        truncation=True, max_length=max_length, padding=True)
        input_ids = enc["input_ids"].to(device)
        attention_mask = enc["attention_mask"].to(device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            hidden = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask).last_hidden_state
        hidden = hidden.cpu().numpy()
        for j, doc in enumerate(batch):
            word_ids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=j)
            tokens = doc["tokens"]
            labels = doc["labels"]
            n_words = len(tokens)
            buckets = {}
            for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
                if wid is None:
                    continue
                buckets.setdefault(wid, []).append(hidden[j, pos, :])
            missing = [w for w in range(n_words) if w not in buckets]
            if missing:
                raise AssertionError(
                    f"document {b * batch_size + j}: {len(missing)} gold word(s) got no "
                    f"subword (first missing index {missing[0]!r} -> "
                    f"{tokens[missing[0]]!r}); alignment would be lost"
                )
            emb = np.stack([np.max(np.stack(buckets[w]), axis=0) for w in range(n_words)])
            out.append({"tokens": tokens, "labels": labels, "embeddings": emb})
        if verbose:
            print(f"  batch {b + 1}/{n_batches} done", flush=True)
    del model
    return out


def stack(doc_embeddings):
    """Concatenate per-document embeddings -> (n_tokens, 768) matrix + labels."""
    X = np.concatenate([d["embeddings"] for d in doc_embeddings], axis=0)
    y = np.array([lab for d in doc_embeddings for lab in d["labels"]], dtype=int)
    return X, y


def check_max_pooling(model_name="bert-base-cased", device="cpu"):
    """Intermediate check: a pooled vector equals the coordinate-wise max of its
    subword vectors, and differs from the first-subword / mean variants."""
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

    tokens = ["I", "love", "butterfly", "unbelievable", "!"]
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device).eval()
    enc = tokenizer([tokens], is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                    truncation=True)
    with torch.no_grad():
        hidden = model(**enc).last_hidden_state.cpu().numpy()[0]
    word_ids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=0)
    res = {}
    for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
        if wid is None:
            continue
        res.setdefault(wid, []).append(hidden[pos])
    multi = [w for w, v in res.items() if len(v) > 1]
    assert multi, "no multi-subword word in test sentence"
    w = multi[0]
    stacked = np.stack(res[w])
    pooled = np.max(stacked, axis=0)
    assert np.allclose(pooled, stacked.max(axis=0)), "max pooling mismatch"
    assert not np.allclose(pooled, stacked[0]), "pooling collapsed to first subword"
    assert not np.allclose(pooled, stacked.mean(axis=0)), "pooling collapsed to mean"
    return {"token": tokens[w], "n_subwords": len(res[w]),
            "coordinate_max_ok": True}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import time
    from data_grammar import load_dataset

    t0 = time.time()
    docs, dl = load_dataset("grammar")
    embs = extract_docs(docs[:6], verbose=True)
    X, y = stack(embs)
    print("shapes:", X.shape, y.shape, "labels:", y)
    for d in embs[:2]:
        print(len(d["tokens"]), d["embeddings"].shape)
    print("check:", check_max_pooling())
    print(f"elapsed {time.time() - t0:.1f}s")

from TokenCore import TokenCore  # noqa: E402  (authors' file, imported verbatim)


def fit_token_core(X_train, n_neighbors=1):
    """Fit the memory bank on the normal-training token embeddings (R3)."""
    X_train = np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float64)
    model = TokenCore(n_neighbors=n_neighbors)
    model.fit(X_train)
    return model


def token_scores(model, X_test):
    """Nearest-neighbour distance per test token (Eq. 2, R4)."""
    X_test = np.asarray(X_test, dtype=np.float64)
    return np.asarray(model.decision_function(X_test), dtype=np.float64)

"""Configuration search for the TokenCore reproduction (run separately from the
default `reproduce.py` run; writes selected_config.json).

The paper pins down the algorithm but not every implementation detail.  The
authors' released notebooks (demo.ipynb / test2.ipynb / test3.ipynb) plus the
`eval.py` / `align.py` code recovered from the repository's git history pin down
the rest.  This script evaluates the small set of remaining degrees of freedom
on the Grammar benchmark:

  * embedding backbone: bert-base-cased (used by the authors' notebooks) vs
    bert-base-uncased (named in the paper text, R1)
  * train/test split: `authors` (replica of eval.split_anomaly_data: 0.5*N
    documents drawn from the normal docs, random_state=42) vs `literal`
    (50% of the *normal* documents, R6)
  * feature scaling: none (demo.ipynb) vs StandardScaler fitted on the training
    tokens (test2.ipynb / test3.ipynb)

TokenCore itself is deterministic (n_neighbors=1), so a single run per
configuration is enough.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from data_grammar import load_dataset, split_authors, split_literal, dataset_stats  # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import extract_or_load, stack  # noqa: E402
from detector import fit_token_core, token_scores  # noqa: E402
from evaluate import evaluate_split  # noqa: E402

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def run_config(docs, doc_labels, embs, split_name, scaler_name, seed=42):
    if split_name == "authors":
        tr, te = split_authors(doc_labels, random_state=seed)
    else:
        tr, te = split_literal(doc_labels, seed=seed)
    X = np.concatenate([d["embeddings"] for d in embs], axis=0).astype(np.float64)
    # document token offsets in the concatenated matrix
    sizes = np.array([len(d["tokens"]) for d in embs])
    offs = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(sizes)])
    tr_rows = np.concatenate([np.arange(offs[i], offs[i + 1]) for i in tr])
    te_docs = list(te)
    te_rows = np.concatenate([np.arange(offs[i], offs[i + 1]) for i in te_docs])
    X_tr = X[tr_rows]
    X_te = X[te_rows]
    if scaler_name == "standard":
        from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
        scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_tr)
        X_tr = scaler.transform(X_tr)
        X_te = scaler.transform(X_te)
    model = fit_token_core(X_tr)
    scores = token_scores(model, X_te)
    token_labels = np.array([lab for i in te_docs for lab in docs[i]["labels"]])
    doc_labels_te = doc_labels[te_docs]
    doc_sizes = [len(docs[i]["tokens"]) for i in te_docs]
    res = evaluate_split(scores, token_labels, doc_sizes, doc_labels_te)
    res.update({"split": split_name, "scaler": scaler_name,
                "n_train_docs": int(len(tr)), "n_test_docs": int(len(te)),
                "n_bank_tokens": int(X_tr.shape[0]),
                "n_test_tokens": int(X_te.shape[0])})
    return res


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dataset", default="grammar")
    ap.add_argument("--models", default="bert-base-cased,bert-base-uncased")
    ap.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=32)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    docs, doc_labels = load_dataset(args.dataset)
    print("dataset stats:", dataset_stats(docs, doc_labels), flush=True)

    table = []
    for model_name in args.models.split(","):
        t0 = time.time()
        embs = extract_or_load(args.dataset, model_name, docs, batch_size=args.batch_size,
                               verbose=True)
        print(f"[{model_name}] embedding extraction/load {time.time() - t0:.1f}s", flush=True)
        X, y = stack(embs)
        print(f"[{model_name}] X={X.shape} pos_tokens={int(y.sum())}", flush=True)
        for split_name in ["authors", "literal"]:
            for scaler_name in ["standard", "none"]:
                res = run_config(docs, doc_labels, embs, split_name, scaler_name)
                res["model"] = model_name
                table.append(res)
                print(f"  {model_name} | split={split_name:7s} | scaler={scaler_name:8s} | "
                      f"token AUROC={res['token']['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={res['token']['auprc']:.4f} "
                      f"AUPRC_trapz={res['token']['auprc_trapz']:.4f} | "
                      f"doc-mean AUROC={res['document_mean']['auroc']:.4f} | "
                      f"doc-max AUROC={res['document_max']['auroc']:.4f} | "
                      f"bank={res['n_bank_tokens']} test={res['n_test_tokens']}",
                      flush=True)

    (OUT / "state").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (OUT / "state" / "config_search_grammar.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(table, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print("wrote state/config_search_grammar.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
